🧠 Crypto News Brief: Extreme fear grips crypto as Bitcoin sinks to an 11-week low and ETF redemptions mount. Washington pulls both ways: Treasury cuts off MEXC and drops a surveillance rule, while a crypto-in-401(k) rule reaches the White House. 🚫 US Treasury Cuts MEXC Off From the US Financial System FinCEN has designated MEXC Global a primary money laundering concern and ordered US financial institutions to stop processing any transfers to or from the exchange. Treasury alleges the top-20 platform handled at least $16 billion in illicit flows between May 2021 and May 2026, tied to sanctions evasion, cybercrime and networks linked to Iran and North Korea. The order takes effect 30 days after publication in the Federal Register. Read full story 📉 Bitcoin ETFs Bleed $412M as BTC Sinks to 11-Week Low US spot Bitcoin ETFs lost $412 million on November 6, a second straight day of heavy redemptions, with BlackRock's IBIT accounting for about $403 million while Fidelity's FBTC was the lone fund with inflows. Ether ETFs shed another $93 million, and year-to-date Bitcoin ETF flows have now slipped into negative territory as BTC hovers near $75,000–$76,000 after an AI-stock selloff. More details 🏦 Crypto in 401(k) Plans Moves Closer as Rule Reaches White House The US Department of Labor has sent a proposed rule to the White House's regulatory review office that would open 401(k) retirement plans to alternative assets, including crypto, following President Trump's executive order. The rule would set criteria for fiduciaries weighing higher costs against diversification and long-term returns, a push Senators Elizabeth Warren and Bernie Sanders have opposed. Read more 🏛️ Treasury Withdraws $250 Crypto Travel Rule Proposal FinCEN and the Federal Reserve have rescinded a 2020 proposal that would have cut the travel-rule reporting threshold for transfers from $3,000 to $250, citing its age and how much the crypto industry has changed. Coin Center and the Crypto Council for Innovation welcomed the move, which follows October's withdrawal of proposed rules on self-hosted wallets and crypto mixing. See details 🕵️ Binance Hackers Swap $124M in Stolen Altcoins Into Bitcoin Elliptic says the North Korea-linked attackers behind the $6.43 billion Binance breach have converted roughly $124 million in altcoins into BTC, routing funds through more than 20,000 wallets

**Welcome back!** It’s recap day, with this week’s five biggest stories and five tools to try this weekend. Claude started turning down requests to copy existing games, and OpenAI revealed the hidden model behind its recent hacks. ChatGPT learned to talk about your money, and days later Claude asked for a look at your bank account too. And Codex pushed so much code that OpenAI had to rebuild Git to keep up.

**In today's Generative AI Newsletter:**

* **Games:** What kind of game will Claude refuse to build?

* **OpenAI:** Which model was behind OpenAI’s hacks?

* **ChatGPT:** Can you ask ChatGPT out loud where your paycheck went?

* **Claude:** Why does Claude want to see your bank account?

* **Git:** Why did OpenAI have to rebuild Git?


----------







----------
## Claude stopped building copycat games

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/1fb8e6e3-1891-4dfb-be35-e8d8576820ab/a34970ce-fbda-4190-b1f7-0eee0bd7abe2.jpg?t=1793607591)
Caption: 

Claude Code now [turns you down](https://www.gamedeveloper.com/programming/anthropic-appears-to-have-ordered-ai-tool-claude-to-stop-remaking-video-games) if you ask it to build a game that sounds too much like one that already exists. Anthropic confirmed the change, saying that copying someone else’s game breaks its usage rules.

In recent weeks, several indie studios had pulled their public demos, worried that someone would hand them to an AI and release a copy first.

The rule caught more than copycats. One studio that makes digital board-wargame modules for paying customers says Claude started refusing its work right after it asked whether the new rule covered it.

Then Anthropic [softened the rule](https://www.tomshardware.com/tech-industry/artificial-intelligence/anthropic-loosens-game-restrictions-claude-will-now-offer-to-build-original-game-in-same-genre-if-asked-to-copy), and Claude now offers to build an original game in the same genre instead.


----------

Автор: Financial Times

Dear readers, Democrats won a decisive victory in the blue tsunami that swept through America in the midterm elections this week. But the biggest victory was for American democracy, which proved, once again, its remarkable ability to self-correct, even in the face of the most brutal Trumpian assault.  For the past two years, we’ve watched with astonishment Donald Trump’s attempts to undermine the rule of law, degrade the political discourse and punish friends as well as foes. On Tuesday Americans said they’d had enough of him and his policies, which have driven up the cost of living and enriched cronies. As the results came in, vice-president JD Vance, who is likely to be running in 2028, acknowledged what has been obvious for many months: that the Iran war and its impact on fuel prices was a determining factor in voters’ shift to the left.  To tell the story of how Democrats flipped both the House and the Senate, our reporters scattered across various states, our data journalists pored over the results, and our commentators analysed the outcome. As our editorial board concluded, there are two main risks now: the first is that a frustrated Trump doubles down on misguided adventures, whether in Iran or elsewhere; the second is that the Democrats squander this victory with infighting and attempts to extract revenge. With two more years to go until the presidential election, the midterms were only the beginning of the end of Trump.  My choices this week Of course, the economy was not Trump’s only downfall. The blue tsunami was also fuelled by mounting opposition to AI data centres, and went on to trigger a powerful tech market rout. (Wall Street stocks steadied on Friday.) As our reporters explain, Silicon Valley’s elites now have a big task on their hands: rebuilding their relationship with the American public. The hacking of software platform Hugging Face by OpenAI agents in July was the starkest warning yet that the very capabilities that make AI agents useful — autonomy, persistence and collaboration — also enable them to bypass safeguards. In this visual story, we piece together the hack and take you inside the race to keep AI under control. In just four years, Arini Capital Management went from a $1bn hedge fund start-up to a $22bn investment firm. Now, the firm is fighting to hold on to its bets amid a brutal sell-off in the riskiest reaches of corpo
